chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a wall that three persons collaborated to demolish: it fell upon one of them and he died. So he held the remaining two liable for his blood money (diya), because each one of them is responsible for his companion.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.دِيَة: Diya — blood money, the financial compensation owed for accidental or quasi-intentional killing
key_terms.ضَامِن: Guarantor/liable party (damin) — one who bears legal responsibility for harm caused
key_terms.قَضَى: Judicial ruling (qada') — a formal legal judgment, not merely an opinion

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on blood money when multiple people jointly demolish a wall that kills one of them?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling by Imam Ali (AS) — transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) — establishing collective liability in joint demolition accidents. When three men collaborated to demolish a wall and it fell on one, killing him, Imam Ali ruled the two survivors must pay the full diya. The juridical principle invoked — that each co-participant is mutually responsible for his fellow — became a foundational maxim in Shia fiqh for cases of joint harmful acts.
word_analysis: so he held liable/imposed liability upon

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding three who had participated is demolishing it upon one of them, so he died. So the remaining ones had to take the responsibility for his wergild because each one of them was responsible for his companion’.
